title: The impact of architectural form on physiological stress: a systematic review
review_question: To identify (i) the clinical biomarkers used to measure physiological stress responses to architectural form, (ii) categories of architectural forms that are correlated with elevated stress response, and (iii) limitations with existing research methods.
inclusion_exclusion_criteria: Controlled studies evaluating physiological stress responses to individual architectural forms (geometric shape/configuration of interior built environment) using clinical biomarkers. Excluded: studies on lighting, materiality, thermal comfort, color, street design, biophilia, urban greenery, indoor plants, or grouped intervention characteristics. Population: healthy individuals. Outcome: clinical biomarkers (EEG, fMRI, HRV, GSR, pupil dilation, salivary cortisol), excluding self-reported stress. Both virtual and physical environments considered. Language: English. Date: January 2013 to January 2023.

synthesis_conclusions: Certain architectural forms (curvature, enclosure, proportion) may impact physiological stress responses.
Clinical biomarkers (EEG, fMRI, HRV, GSR, pupil dilation, salivary cortisol) can be used to measure the impact of architectural form on physiological stress.

Minimal wall curvature, narrow spaces, and higher degrees of enclosure (lower ceiling heights, smaller window ratios, length-to-width aspect ratios > 1) are correlated with elevated physiological stress responses.
The findings for curvature and proportion are not robust due to limited studies and inconsistent definitions.
The field of neuroarchitecture is nascent, and further research is needed to substantiate links between architectural forms and physiological stress outcomes.
evidence_gaps: Paucity of research examining the impact of architectural form on physiological stress responses.
Lack of uniformity in the definition and measurement of architectural forms.
Unisensory approach (VR/2D images) may not capture the multisensory nature of physical architecture.
Focus on acute, short-term physiological responses, neglecting long-term impacts and allostatic overloading.
Need for standardized metrics to define architectural forms.
Need for longitudinal studies to assess long-term exposure impacts.
heterogeneity_sources: Lack of uniformity in the definition and measurement of architectural forms.
Unisensory approach of research methodologies (VR/2D images).
limitations: Limited amount of research in the field.
Lack of uniformity in the definition and measurement of architectural forms.
Reliance on virtual reality and 2D images may not capture multisensory nature and can induce cybersickness.
Focus on acute, short-term physiological responses, not long-term impacts or allostatic overloading.

theory_commitments.specific_claim: Environments with certain architectural forms (e.g., natural-like, curvilinear) can facilitate restoration of directed attention and reduce stress.
Exposure to certain architectural forms (e.g., those incorporating natural elements or curvilinear designs) can lead to physiological and psychological stress reduction.
Human innate tendency to connect with nature influences preferences for architectural forms that mimic natural patterns, leading to reduced stress.

mechanism_chain.description: A proposed causal mechanism linking architectural form (e.g., minimal wall curvature) to physiological stress.

instruments_used.name: Heart Rate Variability (HRV)
instruments_used.description: Measures variations in the time interval between heartbeats, indicative of physiological stress and relaxation.

instruments_used.name: Cortisol levels
instruments_used.description: Measured from saliva or blood samples to assess physiological stress response.

instruments_used.name: Skin Conductance Response (SCR) / Electrodermal Activity (EDA)
instruments_used.description: Measures changes in electrical conductance of the skin, reflecting sympathetic nervous system activity.

instruments_used.name: Blood Pressure
instruments_used.description: Measures systolic and diastolic blood pressure.

instruments_used.name: Perceived Stress Scale (PSS)
instruments_used.description: A widely used self-report questionnaire assessing the degree to which situations in one's life are appraised as stressful.

instruments_used.name: Positive and Negative Affect Schedule (PANAS)
instruments_used.description: A 20-item self-report mood scale measuring positive and negative emotional states.

environmental_features: spatial configuration (e.g., open-plan vs. enclosed, complex vs. simple)
material textures (e.g., natural vs. artificial, rough vs. smooth)
lighting conditions (e.g., natural light, color temperature)
presence of natural elements (e.g., plants, views to nature)
control_conditions: different architectural forms (e.g., high vs. low curvature, natural vs. artificial materials)
